key_insight: Increasing compressibility suppresses bluff-body oscillations during lock-in but amplifies them in the second desynchronized regime, revealing a shared response across transverse and rotary motions.
engineering_relevance: Compressibility can either moderate or intensify flow-induced motion, so vibration assessments must account for the body's synchronization regime.
method: Two-dimensional direct numerical simulations at free-stream Mach numbers 0.1–0.6.
Undamped transverse vibration of a circular cylinder at Re = 150 and rotary oscillation of an elliptic cylinder at Re = 200 with aspect ratio 0.5.
Comparison across first desynchronized, synchronous lock-in, and second desynchronized regimes.
evidence_signal: Simulations show reduced amplitudes, fluctuating aerodynamic coefficients, and hysteretic jumps during lock-in, while second-desynchronized amplitudes increase with Mach number following a modified Prandtl–Glauert relationship in both cases.
watch_item: The findings come from two-dimensional, low-Reynolds-number simulations; persistence at higher Reynolds numbers remains unverified.
paper_title: Compressibility effects on the flow-induced motions of bluff bodies: common features from transverse and rotary oscillations
